title: add downgrade guard, backup/restore, and schema migration safety for private-installer
author: Eleni K. Morales
description: Motivation: Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) saw two incidents during minor rollbacks where mismatched schema versions and missing backups caused service disruption. This PR implements three safety features for the private-installer and Helm/Terraform artifacts: 1) downgrade guard: prevents applying a release that would downgrade critical components or DB schema; 2) backup/restore hooks: automated pre-upgrade full backup of DB and object storage and a documented restore path; 3) schema migration safety: migration plan tagging and a runtime compatibility check to avoid destructive down-migrations. This is intended to be a release-blocking change for v1.18 private installs to reduce rollback risk. What changed (high level): - private-installer: add pre-upgrade backup job and post-upgrade verification steps, and runtime check to abort if target version < pinned minimal version. - helm charts (private/helm): introduce chart hooks for pre-upgrade backups, values to enable/disable, and versionPin constraint fields. - terraform modules (private/terraform): add version_pinning variable and plan-time checks that fail plan/apply if a downgrade is detected. - db migrations: introduce migration metadata files with semantic migration IDs and backwards_compatible flags. Installer consults this metadata before applying migrations. - docs: upgrade/rollback runbook and playbook for restores under private deployments. Checklist: - [x] Add pre-upgrade backup job and test for Postgres + object store (S3/GCS compat) - [x] Add downgrade guard checks at plan/apply and Helm upgrade time - [x] Add migration metadata and preflight checks - [x] Update private-installer logs and metrics to emit upgrade intent and backup status - [x] Add unit/integration tests for guard logic and backup hooks - [x] Add runbook and upgrade playbook entries (docs/private/restore.md) Backwards compatibility and rollout: The new checks are opt-out via values for air-gapped customers that cannot reach object storage during maintenance windows. Default behavior is on for all new upgrades. Existing clusters will pick up new checks when operators update the installer binary or Helm chart; no automated forced upgrades are performed. Usage notes: See docs/private/restore.md for step-by-step restore, and chart values under private/helm/values-upgrade.yaml for toggles. Example helm command: helm upgrade --install redwood-private ./charts/private -f values-upgrade.yaml --namespace redwood --wait References: Linear ENG-7821 (upgrade safety), ENG-7899 (private-installer runbook), incident notes SUP-4567.

Eleni K. Morales: Responded - added backup_timeout to values-upgrade.yaml and emitted metrics.private_upgrade_backup_seconds and metrics.private_backup_bytes_total.
Marcus Lin: Requested change - Terraform plan should fail fast on downgrade detection instead of continuing and erroring later. Also expand test matrix to include major/minor version skew.
Eleni K. Morales: Updated terraform module to fail during validation and added unit tests for skew detection. Added test cases for major/minor skew in CI.
Omar Rafi: Approved after verifying Helm hook idempotency and post-upgrade verification; ran integration job against a staging cluster and observed successful backup/restore cycle.
CI Bot: initial run failed (integration-upgrade-tests) due to timing flakiness in backup job; re-triggered and passed on rerun. All checks green.

release_notes: Add pre-upgrade backup hooks, downgrade guards, and migration metadata to improve safety of private deployments during upgrades. Opt-out via chart/terraform flags for air-gapped customers.
